headline: US waives Iran sanctions for 60 days after peace talks
summary: The move follows a nascent peace deal aimed at ending hostilities in the region, including a lull in fighting in Lebanon.
details: The United States has waived sanctions on Iran for 60 days starting Monday, following the first round of talks under a new peace deal. Officials report a sustained lull in fighting in Lebanon as part of an agreement to end regional hostilities.

The developments come after a weekend of tension, including threats from US President Donald Trump to restart the war if Iran disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Tanker traffic has since resumed and global oil prices have declined.

US Vice-President JD Vance reported that talks in Switzerland, mediated by Pakistan and Qatar, laid a good foundation for a final peace deal. However, Iran's Foreign Ministry has denied that nuclear program discussions have begun.

The interim agreement includes a roadmap toward a permanent deal within 60 days. It also establishes a mechanism to end fighting in Lebanon between Israel and Hezbollah, and opens a communication line for safe ship passage through the Strait of Hormuz.

As part of the economic relief, the US Treasury allows Tehran to sell oil and related products and receive payments until August 21. US officials suggest unfrozen Iranian funds may be used to purchase US agricultural products like corn, soy, and wheat.

President Trump warned that he will 'do what I have to do' if Iran does not live up to the agreement or behaves poorly. He emphasized that Iran must agree to weapons inspections to ensure 'nuclear honesty.'
While Israel was not a party to the peace agreement, it has agreed to a new ceasefire in Lebanon. Lebanese officials report that intense fighting has abated since Saturday night.

headline_marked: Israel says [[military operations in Lebanon will continue]]
headline: Israel says military operations in Lebanon will continue
summary: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and top defense officials vow to maintain strict measures to counter threats from Lebanon.
details: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has announced that military operations in Lebanon will continue. This statement comes as Israel seeks to neutralize threats emerging from the region.
In a joint press conference, Defense Minister Israel Katz and Chief of Staff Lieutenant General Yair Zamir stated that strict measures will be maintained to counter any threat coming from Lebanon.
The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) will continue working to destroy terrorist infrastructure and maintain a security zone in southern Lebanon to protect both soldiers and civilians.
Officials emphasized that the security of Israel's civilian population and military personnel is the highest priority and will not be compromised under any circumstances.
Prime Minister Netanyahu, the Defense Minister, and the Chief of Staff also held a phone call with top officials of the Northern Command to coordinate ongoing operations.
caption:
Israel vows to continue its military campaign in Lebanon to destroy terrorist infrastructure.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has announced that military operations in Lebanon will continue. This statement comes as Israel seeks to neutralize threats emerging from the region.

In a joint press conference, Defense Minister Israel Katz and Chief of Staff Lieutenant General Yair Zamir stated that strict measures will be maintained to counter any threat coming from Lebanon.

The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) will continue working to destroy terrorist infrastructure and maintain a security zone in southern Lebanon to protect both soldiers and civilians.

Officials emphasized that the security of Israel's civilian population and military personnel is the highest priority and will not be compromised under any circumstances.

Prime Minister Netanyahu, the Defense Minister, and the Chief of Staff also held a phone call with top officials of the Northern Command to coordinate ongoing operations.
